query: How much of provincial cradle-to-gate GWP is attributable to transport versus on-site activities and open burning, and which mapping metrics best identify transport and burning hotspots?

response.query: How much of provincial cradle-to-gate GWP is attributable to transport versus on-site activities and open burning, and which mapping metrics best identify transport and burning hotspots?
response.answer: Transport typically accounts for a significant portion of provincial cradle-to-gate GWP, often more than on-site activities and open burning. Mapping metrics like emission factors and distance traveled best identify transport hotspots, while fuel consumption and waste generation identify burning hotspots.

results.title: Comparison of the use of life cycle assessment and ecological ...
results.content: # Comparison of the use of life cycle assessment and ecological footprint methods for evaluating environmental performances in dairy production. Life Cycle Assessment and Ecological Footprint together enables a comprehensive assessment of environmental sustainability. The aim of the study was the comparison between LCA and EF in assessing the environmental performances of milk production, assuming as case study three cattle farms with increasing levels of production intensity. Adopting GWP as a metric, the results per kg of FPCM provided by the LCA highlighted a different trade off compared to the EF method: the farm with the highest productive intensity produced the least impactful milk in terms of GWP but had the most negative Ecological Balance (EB). The LCA method evaluates impacts intensity referred to a specific functional unit and its results are strongly influenced by productive efficiency; the EF method evaluates environmental sustainability of productions in relation to the territory that supports them.
